data.title: bn-ybq: CML elaborator with pre-charged output budget (supersedes cr-35xovl)

data.body: [risk:high] Flat clause lists create an unbounded-depth BoolExpr before validation. lower() sends every init, action-guard, and invariant clause through conjoin (lines 272-277, 319-324, 335-342). conjoin pre-charges only the node count, then fold builds a left-deep Box chain. Each clause passed top_bool separately, so no check covers the combined depth. With the 16 MiB source limit and 1<<20 output budget, untrusted CML can supply hundreds of thousands of individually shallow clauses. Init evaluation or ModelBuilder then rejects after construction, and recursive drop of the deep chain can overflow the process stack instead of returning typed inconclusiveness. Failure modes: stack-overflow abort and service denial during lowering or error cleanup. Edge cases: init, repeated require clauses, and invariant clauses are affected; empty or small lists are safe. Rollback: revert this lowering path, or replace the fold with a pre-bounded balanced construction that remains safe to destroy on every error path. Monitoring: count process aborts and typed OutputTooLarge or ExpressionTooDeep outcomes around CML lowering; alert on worker restarts while handling CML. Validation: add large flat init, guard, and invariant cases in the existing memory-limited, 512 KiB-stack child harness; each must return a typed error or a valid bounded model without abort. This BLOCK is static review metadata and does not satisfy the separate risk:critical human-approval gate.

data.reason: Unresolved risk:high denial of service: lower.rs:473-483 builds unbounded-depth conjunctions from flat untrusted clause lists before any combined-depth check; see th-2e3epd.

data.body: Fixed in ad9d7da. Each lowered node now checks its depth against continuum_model_core's MAX_EXPR_DEPTH before it is built, counted the way BoolExpr::depth and IntExpr::depth count it. So no lowered expression deeper than the builder and evaluator admit is ever constructed or dropped; deeper input is Unlowerable::ExpressionTooDeep. conjoin builds init, guard, and invariant clause lists as a balanced tree (ceil(log2 n) levels over the deepest clause). It checks that combined depth and charges the && nodes before building any of them. The crate-doc inventory gains a depth column for every site, and states that every tree type (expressions, types, lowered expressions) is refused before it exceeds its depth bound, so no drop recurses deeply. Tests, all in the ulimit -v 512 MiB, 512 KiB-stack child harness: flat init, guard, and invariant lists of 100k clauses lower to valid bounded models, and 400k clauses are refused with a typed error. Also: a conjunction over the depth bound is refused, and a deep equivalence nest is refused by depth. Anti-vacuity: with the old left fold restored, the flat-init child dies of stack overflow (checked).
[resolved] The balanced conjoin implementation computes the combined depth and charges all conjunction nodes before construction. The target now prevents the reported left-deep drop path.

data.reason: Fixed at ad9d7da: balanced construction and prechecked combined depth.

data.body: [risk:high] Init lowering bounds candidate count and stored bindings separately, but never bounds their product with predicate cost. Lines 278-283 admit up to 2^22 candidate states after constructing a predicate of up to the 1<<20-node output budget, and lines 290-295 evaluate that entire predicate for each candidate. A small source with 22 binary variables and 100,000 flat false clauses therefore performs hundreds of billions of expression visits before returning NoInitialStates; a mostly true predicate can still perform billions before TooManyInitialStates. Failure modes: synchronous CPU exhaustion, worker starvation, and no timely typed resource result for untrusted CML. Edge cases: false predicates traverse the full domain; accepted states only trip the binding cap after many costly evaluations; small domains or small predicates are safe. Rollback: keep CML lowering unavailable to untrusted callers, or disable exhaustive init enumeration until a combined work budget exists. Monitoring: record candidate evaluations, predicate-node visits, lowering CPU, and worker cancellations; alert when work grows far faster than source size. Validation: add an operation-counted wide-domain plus wide-predicate case that must return InitDomainTooLarge or a new typed work-limit error before enumeration; test boundary products without wall-clock assertions. This BLOCK is static review metadata and does not satisfy the separate risk:critical human-approval gate.

[risk:high] Flat binder lists make name validation quadratic before any time limit can refuse the source. binders() calls check_fresh for every binder here, while check_fresh scans the entire growing scope at lines 859-864. A valid 100,000-name flat quantifier triggers roughly five billion string comparisons while consuming only a fraction of the 16 MiB source and 1<<20-node budgets. The same growing-vector uniqueness pattern exists for record fields at lines 1336-1344. Failure modes: CPU exhaustion and request starvation before a typed elaboration result. Edge cases: many unique flat binders, action or def parameters, and wide record literals/types are affected; duplicate early names and short lists are cheap. Rollback: keep this elaborator unavailable to untrusted service paths until uniqueness checks use an indexed scope; the source feature can remain scaffold-only. Monitoring: record source item counts and elaboration CPU, and alert on superlinear CPU per byte or worker cancellation. Validation: instrument comparison counts for N and 2N unique binders and record fields, require linear growth, and run large flat cases inside the existing resource-limited child harness. This BLOCK is static review metadata and does not satisfy the separate risk:critical human-approval gate.

data.reason: Two unresolved risk:high denial-of-service paths remain: init enumeration lacks a combined predicate-work bound, and flat-name uniqueness checks are quadratic. The separate risk:critical human-approval gate remains required.

data.body: Fixed in b11b18b. Scopes (params, lets, binders) now keep an ordered index by name (elab Scope), and record literals and record types check field uniqueness with an ordered set. So freshness and lookup cost O(log n) comparisons, not a scan. All work is charged to a new work budget, budget::MAX_WORK: each lookup charges the log of its table size, and exhaustion is ElabErrorKind::WorkLimitExceeded. elaborate_source_with reports the Usage spent. Tests count operations, with no wall clock: binder_name_checks_grow_linearly and record_field_checks_grow_linearly (4000 vs 8000, ratio <= 2.4). a_hundred_thousand_binders_elaborate_within_limits runs in the ulimit child and stays under MAX_WORK/64. Anti-vacuity: an honestly charged linear scan put back gives ratios 3.92x (binders) and 3.96x (fields), and both tests fail. The crate-doc inventory now has a work column listing every loop and recursion in elab, types, lower and norm.

Fixed in b11b18b. Before it evaluates any candidate, init enumeration charges lower::init_work: candidates x (predicate size x (variables + 1) + 2 x variables + 1). Over the budget is Unlowerable::WorkLimitExceeded, with nothing enumerated. Each accepted state's builder work (copy, placement, sort) is charged before the copy. lower_with reports the Usage spent. Tests: wide_domain_times_wide_predicate_is_refused_before_enumeration (16 variables x 2000 padding clauses, in the ulimit child): refused typed, having spent less than one unit per candidate. the_work_boundary_is_exact: a work limit equal to the measured usage lowers, one unit less is refused typed, for lowering and for elaboration. Anti-vacuity: with the pre-charge removed, the refusal test fails (the model enumerates and lowers).

[risk:high][resolved] The target replaces scanned scopes with an ordered name index and uses ordered sets for record uniqueness. crates/continuum-cml-elab/src/elab.rs:136-173, 989-1001, 1495-1515, and 1534-1565 remove the reported quadratic scans. crates/continuum-cml-elab/tests/resource_bounds.rs:535-570 adds operation-counted growth and bounded 100,000-binder coverage. No unresolved risk:high path remains.

[risk:high][resolved] crates/continuum-cml-elab/src/lower.rs:339-362 computes and burns the saturated candidate times predicate times variable cost before enumeration. Lines 366-401 charge accepted-state builder work before copies. crates/continuum-cml-elab/tests/resource_bounds.rs:593-652 pins early typed refusal and the exact work boundary. No unresolved risk:high path remains.
